NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is a staged antiscalant dose strategy that increases dose progressively during the CIP interval to target silica polymerization hotspots. Standard practice uses a fixed antiscalant dose, which provides uniform but suboptimal protection. The adjacent technique is constant-dose antiscalant injection; the departure is the time-variable dose profile that matches the expected silica polymerization kinetics. The mechanism attacks the failure by delivering higher doses when silica solubility is lowest (post-CIP recovery phase), directly suppressing the polymerization nucleation that drives scaling.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is silica scaling rate ∝ [SiO₂]² · (dose)⁻¹. A progressive dose increase from 3 ppm to 8 ppm over 6 hours reduces the scaling potential by ~70% at the critical post-CIP phase. This is verified by the Arrhenius scaling rate equation: scaling rate = k · exp(-Ea/RT) · [SiO₂]² / [antiscalant], where increasing [antiscalant] nonlinearly suppresses k.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (Compared to standard fixed-dose pump installation):
- (a) Existing antiscalant storage tank (unchanged)
- (b) Standard programmable chemical dosing pump (e.g., 0-10 L/h range) installed on the antiscalant injection line
- (c) Dosing schedule programmed as: 3 ppm (0-2h post-CIP), 5 ppm (2-4h), 8 ppm (4-6h), then return to baseline 3 ppm

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Standard practice: 1 fixed-dose pump row. This intervention: replaces fixed pump with programmable pump (same cost class, same installation burden), adds no new sensors or monitoring, and the schedule change is a parameter adjustment. Operational loss: zero (dosing occurs during normal operation). Burden class: same as standard practice.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install dosing pump with progressive schedule; monitor normalized silica flux (L/m²/h) and differential pressure (psi) across tail elements weekly for 3 months. Instruments: Existing RO performance monitors. Pass/fail: Flux reduction <5% and ΔP increase <10% vs. baseline fixed-dose operation. Kill criterion: flux reduction >15% or ΔP increase >20%. Duration: 12 weeks to capture seasonal variability.
